output:
Short answer
- Pick an LED adjustable task lamp with good efficacy (high lm/W), dimming, and — if you want automation — motion or smart control. From your catalog memory the most relevant match is the "Harbor Task Lamp" (I found that name in the product catalog). I don’t have detailed specs for it in memory, so I recommend checking its LED type, lumen output and energy certifications before buying.

Why that type of lamp
- LEDs use far less electricity than incandescent/halogen for the same usable light and last much longer, so they’re the most energy-efficient choice for offices.
- A focused adjustable task lamp lets you light the work area rather than the whole room, reducing total energy use.
- Dimming, occupancy sensors, or smart scheduling further reduce energy by lowering output or switching off when the desk is unoccupied.

What to check (evidence/verification checklist)
For each lamp you consider (including the Harbor Task Lamp), verify these specs before deciding:
- Bulb type: is it an integrated LED or LED replaceable module? (Claim to check: “LED”)
- Lumen output and wattage (or lm/W). Look for high efficacy—ideally >= 80 lm/W for task lighting; >100 lm/W is better. (Requires verification)
- Dimmability and supported dimmer types (triac/ELV/0–10V/smart app). (Requires verification)
- Color temperature (Kelvin). For offices 3000–4000 K is common; 4000 K gives a cooler, “daylight” feel. (Requires verification)
- Color rendering index (CRI). Aim for CRI ≥ 80 (CRI ≥ 90 for color-critical work). (Requires verification)
- Controls: built-in motion sensor, presence sensor, or compatibility with smart controls/standards (Zigbee, Z-Wave, Wi‑Fi). (Requires verification)
- Certifications: ENERGY STAR or DLC listing (these objectively support energy-efficiency claims). (Requires verification)
- Warranty and rated lifetime (e.g., 25,000+ hours). (Requires verification)
- Physical adjustability and glare control (good optics, shielding, or louvers) for comfortable task lighting. (Can be confirmed from specs/photos)

Evidence I have from memory
- Product names/categories I found in the catalog memory: “desk lamp,” “adjustable desk lamps,” “task lamps,” “Harbor Task Lamp,” and broader “lighting products.” I do not have technical specs, images, or certifications stored for those items. So I can point you toward the Harbor Task Lamp as one to inspect, but I cannot confirm its energy-efficiency without checking its spec sheet.

Suggested next steps
1. Tell me which features matter most (budget, style, smart features, dimming, motion sensor). I’ll prioritize recommendations.
2. I can fetch detailed specs (lumens, watts, CRI, Kelvin, dimming, certifications) for the Harbor Task Lamp and other catalog items if you want — then I’ll compare them against the checklist and give a ranked recommendation.
3. If you prefer, I can recommend exact models that typically meet these goals (e.g., ENERGY STAR LED task lamps with motion sensors and >100 lm/W), but I’ll need permission to reference models outside your catalog memory.

Which path do you want: (A) I pull spec details from your catalog for the Harbor Task Lamp and similar items, or (B) I give a short list of general, high-performing lamp models (not necessarily from your catalog) to consider?
